rule.name: Two hyphens between parentheses or quotation marks to em-dash
rule.description: Two hyphens are an incorrect way to write a dash; the correct form is the em-dash

rule.name: Two hyphens between words to closed em-dash
rule.description: Two hyphens are an incorrect way to write a dash; the correct form is the em-dash

example.before: We -- or you We--or you (US English)

rule.name: Remove spaces before certain punctuation, typically . , : ; ? !
rule.description: No space is placed before certain punctuation marks

rule.name: Convert two periods (..) in parenthesis by ellipsis (…)
rule.description: Two consecutive dots in parentheses or brackets most likely indicate an error and should be replaced with an ellipsis

rule.name: Convert all nonbreaking hyphens to regular hyphens
rule.description: Convert all nonbreaking hyphens to regular hyphens and eventually add them later by specific rule

rule.name: Three hyphens to em-dash
rule.description: Three hyphens to em-dash

example.after: We — or you 1—2 (depending on other Rules there could be en-dash or em-dash)

rule.name: Convert figure dash to dash between letters
rule.description: Converts figure dash U+2012 into standard dash

rule.name: Remove zero-width characters (U+200B–200D)
rule.description: Remove zero-width spaces, zero-width non-joiner and zero-width joiner to make GREP-based search and replace operations more effective

rule.name: Three or four periods to ellipsis (U+2026)
rule.description: Three or four periods to ellipsis

rule.name: Remove all soft hyphens (U+00AD)
rule.description: Remove all soft hyphens (SHY) to make GREP-based search and replace operations more effective

rule.name: Convert double quotation mark into double prime symbol
rule.description: Convert double quotation mark into inch symbol following number (5" > 5″)

example.before: This is 42" display. 3.5" floppy 24" Tool Box (24") or “24"”
example.after: This is 42″ display. 3.5″ floppy 24″ Tool Box (24″) or “24″”

rule.name: Delete space between quotation marks (hairspace could be added consistently in the next step if required)
rule.description: If primary and secondary quotation marks appear consecutively in the text, no spaces are inserted between them (unless this is a deliberate typographical choice)

rule.name: Replace two single quotes ’ ’ with one double quotation mark ” (correct form of quotation marks to by modified in next step)
rule.description: Replace two single quotation marks ’’ (U+2019) to double high-9 quotation mark ” (U+201D)

example.before: word’’ (The change may not be visible, change font style to Typofix EU Special to see the difference)
example.after: word” (The change may not be visible, change font style to Typofix EU Special to see the difference)

rule.name: Replace two single quotes ‘ ‘ with one double quotation mark “ (correct form of quotation marks to be modified in next step)
rule.description: Replace two single quotation marks ‘‘ (U+2018) to double high-6 quotation mark “ (U+201C)

example.before: ‘‘word (The change may not be visible, change font style to Typofix EU Special to see the difference)
example.after: “word (The change may not be visible, change font style to Typofix EU Special to see the difference)

rule.name: Replace two single quotes ‹ ‹ with one double quotation mark « (correct form of quotation marks to be modified in next step)
rule.description: Replace two single left-pointing angle quotation ‹‹ (U+2039) to left-pointing double angle quotation « (U+00AB)

example.before: ‹‹word word‹‹ (The change may not be visible, change font style to Typofix EU Special to see the difference)
example.after: «word word« (The change may not be visible, change font style to Typofix EU Special to see the difference)

rule.name: Replace two single quotes › › with one double quotation mark » (correct form of quotation marks to be modified in next step)
rule.description: Replace two single right-pointing angle quotation ›› (U+203A) to left-pointing double angle quotation » (U+00BB)

example.before: ››word word›› (The change may not be visible, change font style to Typofix EU Special to see the difference)
example.after: »word word» (The change may not be visible, change font style to Typofix EU Special to see the difference)

rule.name: Replace multiple tabs by single tab
rule.description: Multiple tabs are likely a mistake in the text, although they may be part of a legacy table format. In most cases, it is safe to replace them with a single tab (or eventually replace them with a space, or remove them entirely)

rule.name: Remove all kinds of spaces (horizontal and vertical) at the end of the story

category.name: Spaces
Run first – remove extra or double spaces, convert all spaces to standard space (prefs)

example.before: This is the end of story. This is the end of story.
example.after: This is the end of story. This is the end of story.

rule.name: Remove spaces adjacent to a tab
rule.description: Spaces next to tabs serve no purpose in the text and should be deleted

example.before: 20Kč (Czech) 20 mil. Kč (Czech) 20 Sk (Slovak) 1kr. (Danish) 20 DM (German) 15zł (Polish) 20lei (Romanian) 15 Δρχ. / 15 δρχ. (Greek) 70 Ft (Hungarian)
example.after: 20 Kč (Czech) 20 mil. Kč (Czech) 20 Sk (Slovak) 1 kr. (Danish) 20 DM (German) 15 zł (Polish) 20 lei (Romanian) 15 Δρχ. / 15 δρχ. (Greek) 70 Ft (Hungarian)

rule.name: No space between value and currency symbols (7€)
rule.description: No space between value and currency symbols (7€)

rule.name: Nonbreaking space between value and local currency word (20 dollars)
rule.description: Nonbreaking space between value and local or old currency unit expressed in word: Value – nbspace – local currency word (20 dollars, 10 korun, 1 złoty, 5 euros)

example.before: 5euro (many but not all languages) 20korun (Czech, Slovak) 1000 forint körülbelül 3 dollár, 2 font vagy 63 korona (Hungarian) 20 dollars (English) 100euros (French, Spanish, Portuguese, English) 20 Mark (German) 50 markkaa (Finnish) 15 złotych i 10 groszy (Polish)
example.after: 5 euro (many but not all languages) 20 korun (Czech, Slovak) 1000 forint körülbelül 3 dollár, 2 font vagy 63 korona (Hungarian) 20 dollars (English) 100 euros (French, Spanish, Portuguese, English) 20 Mark (German) 50 markkaa (Finnish) 15 złotych i 10 groszy (Polish)

rule.name: Keep together month and year (e.g., June 56, October 1956, Year 1968)

example.before: Listopad 1989 (Czech) jaro 68 nebo podzim 1989 (Czech) août 99 (French) printemps 1999 (French) April 45 (English, German…) Iunie 1985, Martie‘60, anul2000 (Romanian) Kolovoz 2025. (Croatian) Júl 1999 a jeseň 2000 (Slovak)

rule.name: Keep together historical date shorthand (e.g., June ’56, October ’56)
rule.description: The abbreviated version of the year is indicated with a correct apostrophe and separated from the month or season by a non-breaking space to prevent the expression from being split at the end of a line

example.before: Czerwiec ‘56 (Polish) Listopad'89 (Czech, Polish) Roku‘88 (Czech, Polish) août `99 (French) April ´45 (English, German…) Decembrie '89 (Romanian) Anni '80 (Italian) Годината ‘80 (Bulgarian) Október ‘67 (Slovak)
example.after: Czerwiec ’56 (Polish) Listopad ’89 (Czech, Polish) Roku ’88 (Czech, Polish) août ’99 (French) April ’45 (English, German…) Decembrie ’89 (Romanian) Anni ’80 (Italian) Годината ’80 (Bulgarian) Október ’67 (Slovak)

rule.name: Keep date and month name together (2 May)
rule.description: Insert a nonbreaking space in dates in this format: # Month

rule.name: Keep short dates with periods together without spaces (MDY 12.11.1974)
rule.description: The short date format is written with non-breaking spaces to prevent the expression from being split at the end of a line

rule.name: Keep short dates with slashes together without spaces MDY (12/11/1974)
rule.description: Keep short dates with slashes together without spaces MDY (12/11/1974)

rule.name: Keep month with day number together in this format: Month #
rule.description: A non-breaking space is inserted between the name of the month and the day number to prevent the expression from being split at the end of a line

rule.name: Convert short days with periods to slash (12/27)
rule.description: Convert short days with periods to slash MD (12.27. -> 12/27)

rule.name: Convert period to preferred separator in dates (slash, hyphen)
rule.description: Convert period to preferred separator in dates DMY (slash, hyphen) – 11/1/2024 or 11-1-2024

rule.name: Convert period to preferred separator in dates (slash, hyphen)
rule.description: Convert period to preferred separator in dates MDY (slash, hyphen) – 01/13/2024 or 01-13-2024

rule.name: Convert hyphen to preferred separator in dates (slash, period)
rule.description: Convert hyphen to preferred separator in dates MDY (slash, period) – 01/13/2024 or 01.13.2024

rule.name: Convert slash to preferred separator in dates (hyphen, period)
rule.description: Convert slash to preferred separator in dates MDY (hyphen, period) – 01-13-2024 or 01.13.2024

rule.name: Convert short days with hyphen to slash (12/27)
rule.description: Convert short days with hyphen to slash MD (12-27 -> 12/27)

rule.name: En-dash between date ranges in various formats ending with year (1898 or 89 or ’89)
rule.description: En-dash without spaces between date ranges in various formats (1.2.2020–1.3.2026). Many other forms are supported (1.–2. April 2025, 1. X.–2. XII. or 1. 9.–10. 9. ’87)

rule.name: En-dash between date ranges in various formats ending with year (1898 or 89 or ’89)
rule.description: En-dash without spaces between date ranges in various formats (1 December 2026). Many other forms are supported (1–2 April 2025, 1 X–2 XII)

rule.name: Fix Dublin 6W instead of incorrect 6 W
rule.description: Fix Dublin 6W instead of incorrect 6 W which means 6 Watt

example.before: The Dublin 6 W designation is unusual.

rule.name: Alert: two capital letters at the beginning of a word
rule.description: Two capital letters are not written consecutively at the beginning of a sentence or certain words. However, exceptions may be made for company names, product names, service names, or intentional neologisms.

example.before: EXample of the PRoblem. (Incorrect English) Example of the Problem. (Correct English)

rule.name: Alert: two consecutive identical parentheses or brackets
rule.description: Two identical parentheses in a row are usually incorrect; one of them may be superfluous. However, they may be secondary parentheses, which should have a different form. Or perhaps everything is fine in this particular context.

rule.name: Alert: sentence probably starts with lowercase letter
rule.description: The beginning of a sentence should start with a capital letter. However, it is possible that in a given context, the use of a lowercase letter is correct.

example.before: (Hello.) new sentence. (Incorrect English) (Hello.) New sentence. (Correct English) “Hi!” my name is Judy. (Incorrect English) “Hi!” My name is Judy. (Correct English) Filip, Linda atd. jsou kamarádi. (Correct Czech)

rule.name: Alert: a word followed by hyphen
rule.description: A word followed by hyphen could be intentional (Ein- oder Zweizimmerwohnung) or the hyphen could represent dash or hyphen with or without spaces depending on context and language.

example.before: Ein – oder Zweizimmerwohnung (German incorrect) Ein- oder Zweizimmerwohnung (German correct) Nosotros —o tú-. (Spanish incorrect) Nosotros —o tú—. (Spanish correct) Říkáš- li pravdu… (Czech incorrect) Říkáš‑li pravdu… (Czech) budynki jedno- i dwupiętrowe (Polish correct) motywy staro- i nowotestamentowe (Polish correct) kroje jedno- lub dwuelementowe (Polish correct) układy jedno- i wielopoziomowe (Polish correct) reakcje endo- lub egzotermiczne (Polish correct) mono- i poligamia makro- i mikroekonomia elektro- i gazowe

rule.name: Alert: It is possible that this is an incorrectly typed expression “à la”
rule.description: It is possible that this is an incorrectly typed expression “à la” meaning “in the style of”

example.before: Kuře alá bažant (Czech) Kuře á la bažant (Czech) Kuře alà bažant (Czech)

rule.name: Alert: Two initials connected with hyphen
rule.description: Two initials connected by a hyphen can mean “from–to,” in which case they should be written with a dash.

rule.name: Alert: It is possible that the plus sign (+) is used instead of the † symbol for the date of death.
rule.description: It is possible that the plus sign (+) is used instead of the † symbol for the date of death.

example.before: (* 1928 Budapest, + 2023 Paris) (+2023 in New York) Georges Pompidou (+ 1968) (The spaces between † and year may vary according local preferences.)
example.after: (* 1928 Budapest, † 2023 Paris) (†2023 in New York) Georges Pompidou († 1968) (The spaces between † and year may vary according local preferences.)

rule.name: Alert: a.m. or p.m. following the 24-hour clock
rule.description: It is possible that the plus sign (+) is used instead of the † symbol for the date of death.
